title: MACA FP32 sin/cos library routes admitted on xcore1002 after bounded qualification

evidence.scope: Installed source inspection and isolated native CPU compilation. GPU visibility was empty; no device numerical evaluation or provider call occurred. The first failed preparation and its frozen source remain preserved.

observation: The installed MetaX backend redirects libdevice to a CUDA-compatible Python API, but explicitly links MACA bitcode libraries. FP32 sin/cos compile to MCFATBIN under the declared xcore1000 native family. C1 only admits OCML trig emission on HSACO. The missing MACA route is a software lowering boundary, not evidence that the device lacks a math path. Numerical behavior remains unmeasured by this work.
proposed_change: Register explicit maca.sin.f32 and maca.cos.f32 instructions for the existing FP32 unary operations; emit only their matching MCFATBIN route and admit only direct unary source calls. Keep the real Target unchanged until original-domain device evidence supports a reviewed successor declaration. Preserve the RoPE factory's scaled inv_freq and custom scalar value rather than applying scaling again or changing its tensor ABI.
promotion_disposition: Admit only maca.sin.f32 and maca.cos.f32 on exact xcore1002 using the retained bounded component and original RoPE qualification. TF32 remains unadmitted. Earlier source-preparation, IEEE RoPE and TF32 failures retain their original verdicts. No exhaustive FP32 precision, general TF32 implementation, other-SDK support or performance claim is promoted.

principles_review.P1_P3: Reuse existing lm.sin/lm.cos and the one canonical scalar-specialization boundary; introduce no alternate IR operation or layout model.
principles_review.P2_P8: Name the MACA contract separately and expose the actual library call and native object route.
principles_review.P4_P5_P7: Reuse unary FP32 typing/effects and register operation/dtype ownership; code-object checks and restricted source admission accompany emission. Existing cost coverage continues to report uncounted transcendental arithmetic.
principles_review.P6: Focused contract tests and unchanged Corpus expectations verify software behavior; native CPU compilation and device numerical evidence remain separate gates.
